content.value_statement: Cold-email programs lose consistency when prospect research, replies, and campaign reviews happen irregularly. This skill organizes weekly tasks and metric comparisons into a repeatable Monday, Wednesday, and Friday workflow.
actual_capabilities: Structure Monday prospect research around configured signal anchors, with signals no older than 14 days.
Coordinate companion list-quality checks and recommend send volume using warm-up status, reply trends, and available personalization time.
Coordinate Wednesday drafting, reviewer checks, spam linting, and handoff to the operator's sending infrastructure.
Organize reply scoring and routing through companion skills and configured operations rules.
Structure Friday metric comparisons against last week and four-week trends, then propose one change for the next week.
Guide quarterly reviews of audience fit, signal freshness, messaging, sending infrastructure, and banned phrases.
limitations: This file is a workflow playbook, not a standalone sending service or background scheduler.
List scoring, drafting, reply scoring, spam linting, and audits depend on companion skills not included in the reviewed file.
Useful recommendations require operator configuration, source access, campaign logs, and reply data.
The playbook does not establish legal compliance, guarantee delivery, or provide verified integrations with prospect sources.

use_cases.title: Manage Founder Outreach
use_cases.description: Plan prospect research, sequence preparation, and weekly reviews around limited personalization time.
use_cases.target_user: Founders running their own outbound program

use_cases.title: Organize Reply Triage
use_cases.description: Prepare a Wednesday queue that separates sales opportunities, positive replies, nurture candidates, and contacts to suppress.

use_cases.title: Review Campaign Performance
use_cases.description: Compare weekly metrics and four-week trends, then choose one measurable adjustment for the next cycle.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Prepare This Week's Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan my cold-email rhythm for this week using the attached configuration and campaign notes. List Monday, Wednesday, and Friday tasks. Identify missing inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a weekly planning session with existing campaign context.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Build the Monday Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Build Monday's queue from these prospect signals, warm-up status, reply trends, and available personalization time. Use available list-quality tools. Flag unverified or stale signals.
prompt_templates.scenario: Refresh prospects and set a realistic weekly send target.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Prepare Wednesday Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare Wednesday's sequence and reply report using these drafts, replies, voice guidance, and routing rules. Use available companion checks. Flag ambiguous replies and failed drafts. Do not send messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review sequence readiness and reply handling before an operator approves sending.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Analyze Friday Trends
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these weekly logs against last week and the four-week trend. Separate missing data from measured results. Recommend exactly one change and its verification metric. Add a quarterly review if due.
prompt_templates.scenario: Select one evidence-based campaign adjustment and assess quarterly drift.

output_examples.input: Prepare Monday's queue. I have two hours for personalization, 25 verified prospects, and an infrastructure limit of 30 sends.
output: Monday queue: Prepare one sequence for 25 verified prospects, within the provided infrastructure limit.
Personalization depth: Deep. Confirm that the available two hours covers all 25 prospects before approval.
List quality: No scoring results were supplied. Check duplicates, role fit, and signal freshness before sending.
Wednesday: Review drafts and triage replies. Friday: Compare results with the previous week.

output_examples.input: Review Friday results: 200 sends, 20 replies, and 8 positive replies. Last week: 200 sends, 16 replies, and 6 positives.
output: Reply rate: 10% this week versus 8% last week.
Positive-reply rate, using sends as the denominator: 4% this week versus 3% last week.
Four-week trend and buy-signal rate: Not available from the supplied data.
Next week's single adjustment: Test one new subject line while keeping targeting and email body unchanged.
Verification metric: Reply rate. The supplied totals cannot identify which messaging pattern caused the improvement.

best_practices: Provide current configuration, verified prospect signals, and complete campaign logs before requesting a weekly review.
Review draft failures, ambiguous replies, suppression decisions, and send limits before approving any infrastructure handoff.
Change one campaign variable per week and define the metric that will verify its effect.
anti_patterns: Treating suggested send volume as permission to bypass infrastructure limits, recipient preferences, or operator approval.
Requesting precise campaign trends without reliable logs or consistent metric definitions.
Changing targeting, subject lines, and messaging simultaneously after a weekly review.

faq.question: What does the weekly workflow cover?
faq.answer: Monday covers signals and list refreshes. Wednesday covers sequence preparation and reply triage. Friday covers metrics and one adjustment.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails automatically?
faq.answer: The file describes a handoff to your sending infrastructure. It contains no standalone sender or background scheduler.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide brand configuration, prospect sources, warm-up status, personalization time, campaign logs, and recent replies. Wednesday drafting also uses voice guidance.

faq.question: Are companion skills required?
faq.answer: The workflow delegates specialized checks to companion skills. Their implementation and referenced scoring scripts were not included in this review.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists all three tools as supported. Actual workflow execution depends on available companion skills, permissions, and campaign inputs.

faq.question: How does the quarterly review differ?
faq.answer: Every 13 weeks, the playbook reviews audience fit, signals, messaging, infrastructure, and banned phrases. It proposes one broader adjustment.
